_note: H9(b): the terrain horizon (item j) checked against an independent NASA product, the average Sun and Earth visibility maps of the lunar south pole (Mazarico et al. 2011, NASA GSFC PGDA product 69, LOLA team). Only the pixels around each point are read (HTTP byte ranges); nothing large is stored. A pixel value is the share of hourly steps over 18.6 years when any part of the disc was visible. This tool's value is the share of hours in its own one-year Horizons table when any part of the disc is above the terrain skyline (disc radius below), so the two periods differ.
credit: Average solar illumination and Earth visibility maps, LOLA Science Team / E. Mazarico, NASA GSFC PGDA (Mazarico et al. 2011, Icarus 211, 1066-1081); LOLA PDS extras (public, no login)
_disc_note: Angular radius seen from the Moon: Sun 696000 km / 149.6e6 km = 0.267 deg; Earth 6371 km / 384400 km = 0.95 deg (mean distances).

extra_points._note: Unnamed engineering point (same as the Horizons check point); not a landing site.

period._note: Same-period check (scripts/pgda_period.py, 15 Nov 2026): the published skylines over 18.6 years of hourly steps, the length of the PGDA simulation, with Sun/Earth angles from the in-browser engine. The PGDA label does not give the dates of its simulation; start is the first date in that label (START_TIME). ridge: the check point where the one-year comparison differs most; its skyline is recomputed with the observer at each listed height and at the 3 x 3 block of points block_offset_m apart (one PGDA pixel); near_km counts the directions where the skyline is set by ground closer than that.
period._headline_note: headline_sites: the two sites named in the one-line summary on the home page (the IM-1 nominal landing area and IM-2). Every other listed site with a terrain skyline is summarised separately (other_sites) and the page says that they differ more.

sample._note: P4q: a larger check of the terrain horizon against the same PGDA maps, at random points (fixed seed) spread evenly over the area south of 80 S (inside the LOLA 80 m grid). Each point gets its own LOLA skyline (scripts/horizon.py ray casting) and Sun/Earth angles from the in-browser engine (src/moonsky.js) over the one-year period of config/ephemeris.json; the PGDA value is the pixel nearest the point and the range of the 3 x 3 pixels around it. Written as the extra block 'pgda_sample' of data/validation.json; the 'pgda' block is not changed.
